name: Cumulative Reasoning
executive_summary: Maintain a growing pool of validated intermediate propositions and build new conclusions only from ones already accepted into that pool — accumulating verified sub-results like a proof, rather than one linear chain.
description: Assigns three roles to the LLM across the process: a proposer suggests new intermediate propositions derived from the current pool, a verifier checks each proposed step's validity before it's accepted into the pool, and a reporter decides when enough has accumulated to produce the final answer. Unlike Tree of Thoughts' branch-and-prune search over competing paths, Cumulative Reasoning builds a single growing directed graph of mutually-consistent validated propositions, closer in spirit to constructing a formal proof step by step. Reported improving accuracy on logical inference tasks (reported gains over existing methods on a curated logical deduction benchmark) and competition-level mathematics (reported solving a notably higher fraction of MATH dataset problems in the hardest difficulty level than prior prompting methods at the time).
when_to_use: Logical deduction or mathematical proof-style tasks where correctness of each intermediate step can be checked before building on it, and accumulating verified sub-results is more natural than committing to one linear guess.
when_not_to_use: Tasks with no natural notion of a checkable intermediate 'proposition' to accumulate — open-ended or creative tasks.
known_pitfalls: Cost is adaptive and grows with how many propositions are proposed and verified before the reporter decides to conclude; needs a stopping rule to bound expense.

primary_source.authors: Zhang, Yu, Wen, Li, Yue, Xie, Zhang, Wan, Yin
primary_source.title: Cumulative Reasoning with Large Language Models
